newsitem.title: CHINA: China criticises EU anti-dumping probe decision.
newsitem.headline: China criticises EU anti-dumping probe decision.

text.p: The European Union's decision to launch anti-dumping investigations against Chinese imports was unwise, the official International Business Daily on Tuesday quoted foreign trade minister Wu Yi as saying.
"The EU's anti-dumping action against Chinese unbleached cloth, shoes and bags is unwise," Wu told visiting French minister of industry, posts and telecommunications Franck Borotra.
The EU has recently stepped up anti-dumping investigations against a number of Chinese products, including major items such as shoes, bags and unbleached cloth.
Chinese officials have said Chinese losses could amount to several billion dollars if the investigations result in actual anti-dumping measures.
They have called on the EU to end what Beijing considers the discriminatory and outdated practice of treating China as a non-market economy.
"Bilateral trade will be damaged if China withdraws from the EU market," International Business Daily quoted Wu Yi as telling Borotra on Monday.
She expressed dissatisfaction with the leading role France had played in pushing some European companies to file anti-dumping charges against Chinese importers, it said.
Paris should treasure the recent improvement in Sino-French ties that had come after a difficult period, Wu said.
China's trade volume with France had reached $4.5 billion in 1995, up by 33.5 percent compared with the previous year. Trade volume in the first nine months of this year was up 10 percent, she said.
Actual investment by French companies in China has reached $1.2 billion involving more than 1,000 projects, she said.
